body.statement: If \(H=0\), \(S=1\), the proxy is the baseline outcome, and \(m_1(x)=x+\Delta_0\) with \(\Delta_0\) equal to the untreated two-period cohort-average mean change, then the functional in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} equals the canonical finite-cohort two-period difference-in-differences estimand. If treatment effects are homogeneous across cohorts and there is no carry-over beyond \(h=0\), then \(\tau_n(z_0)\) reduces to the common contemporaneous finite-cohort average treatment effect on level wealth.
body.justification: Named reductions anchor the new compounded-path object to familiar panel estimands.
body.gap: The banked predecessor did not provide a canonical DID or homogeneous-panel reduction.
body.consumer: Readers can audit the identifying functional against a standard two-period benchmark before using the general event-path result.
body.proof_tex:
Under the first specialization, \(S=1\) and \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\) imply \(\pi_1=1\).  The identifying equality in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and the restriction \(m_1(x)=x+\Delta_0\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_n(z_0)
&=\mathbb E_P[\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_1(z_{01})\\
&=\mathbb E_P[\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-z_{01}-\Delta_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{69}
\]
When the scalar proxy is the event cohort's baseline outcome, \(z_{01}\) is its conditional baseline mean.  When \(\Delta_0\) is the untreated cohort-average post-minus-baseline mean change, (69) is treated post minus treated baseline minus the untreated post-minus-baseline change.  This is precisely the canonical conditional finite-cohort two-period difference-in-differences contrast.

For the second specialization define the cohort effect
\[
\tau_s=\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)-B_{si}(0)\mid z_0,E_0].
\]
Homogeneity across cohorts states that \(\tau_s=\tau^{\mathrm{com}}\) for every \(s\).  By \texttt{def:target} and \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\),
\[
\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\tau_s
=\tau^{\mathrm{com}}\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
=\tau^{\mathrm{com}}.
\tag{70}
\]
The stipulated absence of carry-over beyond \(h=0\) makes this common terminal-level contrast the contemporaneous finite-cohort treatment effect on the level-wealth path defined in \texttt{def:buyhold-level}.  That final causal interpretation uses the stated specialization; it does not follow from the aggregation algebra alone.
